Summary:
Provide a `wl list` CLI flag and a TUI filter to limit returned work items to those with `needs_producer_review` set. By default the filter should show items with the flag set to `true`.

User stories:
- As a Producer, I want to quickly list only items that need my review so I can triage them faster.
- As an operator, I want the default behavior to surface flagged items (true) but allow listing non-flagged items when specified.

Expected behavior / acceptance criteria:
- `wl list` supports a `--needs-producer-review [true|false]` flag. Default behavior: show only items where the flag is `true`.
- TUI provides a filter (e.g., top-level toggle or filter menu) that limits the shown items to flagged ones by default; allow switching to show non-flagged.
- Filtering must be efficient and work with paging/limits.
- Tests and documentation updated describing the CLI flag and TUI filter.

Implementation notes:
- This work item depends on the existence of the `needs_producer_review` field (parent feature).
- Add CLI parsing and apply server-side filtering where possible to avoid transferring unnecessary data.
data.title: Add wl list and TUI filter for items needing producer review

Summary:
Add a single-key binding in the TUI to toggle the `needs_producer_review` flag for a selected work item and add a CLI helper `wl reviewed <work-item-id> [true|yes|false|no]` to set/unset the flag.

User stories:
- As a Producer, I can press a single key in the TUI to mark an item as reviewed (toggle the flag) while working through the queue.
- As a maintainer/automation, I can run `wl reviewed <id> true` or `wl reviewed <id> false` to programmatically set the flag.

Expected behavior / acceptance criteria:
- TUI single-key (suggested: `r`) toggles `needs_producer_review` on the selected item and gives immediate UI feedback.
- New CLI command: `wl reviewed <work-item-id> [true|yes|false|no]` sets the flag accordingly; if not provided, it toggles the existing value.
- Command returns success/failure and updated work item JSON when `--json` is used.
- Tests, docs and help text updated to include the new command and key binding.

Implementation notes:
- Depends on the `needs_producer_review` field being present.
- Ensure permission checks and audit logging for flag changes.
data.title: Add TUI key and  command to toggle needs review flag

data.description:
# Enable batch delete

## Problem statement

`wl delete` accepts only a single work-item id, so removing a set of items
requires one CLI invocation (and one auto-sync) per item. Agents and humans
cleaning up many items therefore pay repeated process-start and sync costs,
making bulk deletion slow and error-prone.

## Users

- **Agents** performing periodic cleanup/pruning of stale or superseded work
  items in batches.
- **Developers/maintainers** tidying a project and wanting to remove several
  related items in one command.

Example user stories:

- As an agent, I want to run `wl delete <id1> <id2> <id3>` so that all three
  items are deleted in one process and a single sync, instead of three
  separate syncs.
- As a maintainer, I want a per-id result summary so I can see which items
  were deleted and which failed, without re-running the command per id.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl delete <id1> <id2> ...` (variadic `<id...>`) deletes every listed work
   item; when exactly one id is supplied the existing output and behaviour are
   unchanged (backward compatible).
2. Each id is processed independently: a failure for one id (not found, invalid
   id) does not abort processing of the remaining ids, and each result is
   reported per-id.
3. The command exits with a non-zero code if any id fails, and zero when all
   ids succeed.
4. Auto-sync runs **exactly once**, after all deletions in the invocation
   complete (consistent with the current single-item behaviour); `--no-sync`
   suppresses it for the whole batch.
5. `--no-recursive` and `--prefix` apply uniformly to every id in the batch;
   with the default (recursive) behaviour, descendants of each parent are
   reported per-id.
6. JSON mode returns a stable per-id `results` array (with an overall
   `success`/`deleted`/`failed` summary) while preserving the existing
   single-id fields (`deletedId`, `deletedWorkItem`, `recursive`) for
   single-id invocations.
7. An integration test file covers: multi-id success, partial failure
   (non-zero exit while other ids still deleted), a single sync for the whole
   batch, `--no-sync`, `--no-recursive`, and single-id backward compatibility.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the soft-delete semantics: deletion still marks items as
  `deleted` (attributed with `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) via
  `db.delete(id, recursive, opts)`; hard-delete/prune remains out of scope.
- The delete command must not begin using a destructive JSONL rewrite or
  bypass existing sync/merge protections.
- Batch processing must not double-delete descendants that are also listed
  explicitly in the same invocation; such ids must be reported coherently
  (skipped / already deleted) rather than producing a hard error.
- Follow existing variadic-id conventions used by `wl update <id...>` and
  `wl close <ids...>` for argument parsing and exit-code semantics.

## Existing state

- `src/commands/delete.ts` registers `program.command('delete <id>')` (single,
  required positional) and performs: id normalisation, existence check,
  descendant collection, `db.delete(...)`, JSON/human output, then one
  best-effort auto-sync guarded by `--no-sync`.
- `wl update <id...>` and `wl close <ids...>` already implement the variadic
  pattern, including per-id `results` arrays, continue-on-error, and non-zero
  exit when any id fails (`src/commands/update.ts`, `src/commands/close.ts`).
- `DeleteOptions` in `src/cli-types.ts` already has `prefix`, `recursive`,
  `sync`.
- `db.delete` is a per-item API
  (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`: `delete(id, recursive = true, opts?)`);
  batch behaviour belongs in the CLI command layer, not the store.
- Existing test `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` asserts the
  single-id JSON shape and auto-sync behaviour, so those fields must remain
  stable.

## Desired change

- Change the command registration to a variadic positional
  (`delete <id...>`) and loop over the ids, mirroring `close`/`update`.
- Normalise and validate each id, collect per-id results, continue on
  per-id errors, and emit a batch summary in JSON mode while retaining the
  single-id JSON shape for a one-id invocation.
- Keep the single auto-sync at the end of the invocation, after all deletions.
- Update `CLI.md` (and any other user-facing delete docs) to document the
  variadic form, per-id results, and exit-code semantics.
- Add focused integration tests for the batch behaviours listed in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — **Primary change.** Switch to `delete <id...>`,
  loop over ids, build per-id results, single terminal sync, partial-failure
  exit code, backward-compatible single-id output.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Extend `DeleteOptions` only if new batch fields are
  needed (likely unchanged; keep minimal).
- `tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts` — **New.** Integration tests for multi-id
  delete, partial failure, single sync, `--no-sync`, `--no-recursive`, and
  single-id backward compatibility.
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — Verify/adjust only if the refactor
  changes shared code paths; single-id expectations must still pass unchanged.
- `CLI.md` — Document the variadic `delete <id...>` form, examples, per-id
  results, and exit-code semantics.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — Read-only reference; no change expected
  (batch orchestration lives in the command layer).

## Related work

- WL-0MKZ4PSF50EGLXLN — "Batch updates" (parent of the `wl update` batch work).
- WL-0MLRSG1HH19G6L4B — "Implement batch processing for 'wl update'" —
  established the variadic-id + per-id-results + continue-on-error pattern to
  mirror.
- WL-0MLRSUXHR000EW60 — "Add unit tests for wl update batch behavior" — test
  conventions for batch CLI behaviour to reuse.
- WL-0MKRPG5FR0K8SMQ8 — "Feature: worklog close (single + multi)" — the other
  existing variadic-id command whose exit-code/output shape is the model.
- WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL — "Recursive deletion of work items with children" —
  defines the recursive descendant behaviour each batch id must preserve.
- WL-0MTFNIRXU007X7U4 — "Delete-side protection: unattributed deletes never
  override live items" and WL-0MTFNIXM3000NFVC — "Attribute real deletes:
  shared delete + CLI/API wiring" — the attribution (`deletedBy`) and sync
  protections the batch path must continue to honour.
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — existing single-delete auto-sync tests
  that must remain green (backward compatibility guard).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: breaking single-id consumers.** Agents and the TUI may parse the
  current single-id JSON (`deletedId`, `deletedWorkItem`, `recursive`).
  *Mitigation*: preserve those fields when exactly one id is supplied; add the
  batch `results` array without removing existing keys; keep the existing
  test file green.
- **Risk: duplicate/descendant ids in one batch** (e.g. deleting a parent and
  one of its children in the same call) causing confusing double-delete
  errors. *Mitigation*: deduplicate repeated ids and treat ids already removed
  as descendants earlier in the batch as skipped/already-deleted in the per-id
  result rather than hard failures (see AC2/Constraints).
- **Risk: sync runs more than once** if the loop naively reuses the current
  post-delete sync block per id. *Mitigation*: restructure so sync is invoked
  once after the loop; test with a multi-id invocation (AC4).
- **Scope-creep risk:** requests to add `--hard`, `--all`, filters, or
  interactive selection during batch delete. *Mitigation*: record extra ideas
  as linked work items; keep this item limited to variadic ids + per-id
  reporting + single sync.
- **Assumption:** `db.delete` remains unchanged and the batch logic is purely
  CLI-layer orchestration.
- **Assumption:** exit-code and per-id-result conventions should match
  `wl update`/`wl close` for consistency.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the intended UX `wl delete <id1> <id2>` (variadic positional ids),
  consistent with `wl update <id...>` and `wl close <ids...>`, with a single
  sync at the end?"
  — Answer: **Assumption (agent, Map), not yet confirmed by producer.** The
  seed description explicitly states "allow commands such as
  `wl delete <id1> <id2>`" and "delete all the items identified before running
  the sync commands", which matches this design. Source: work-item
  description WL-0MUI83ZTX005RN93. *OPEN QUESTION for producer:* confirm the
  variadic-positional UX vs. a `--file`/stdin list input.
- Q: "How should per-id failures and exit codes behave?"
  — Answer: **Assumption (agent, Map):** continue processing remaining ids and
  exit non-zero if any id fails, matching `wl update`/`wl close`. Source:
  `src/commands/update.ts`, `src/commands/close.ts`. *OPEN QUESTION for
  producer:* confirm fail-fast is not preferred.
- Q: "Should single-id output remain backward compatible?"
  — Answer: **Assumption (agent, Map):** yes — preserve existing single-id JSON
  fields to avoid breaking `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` and existing
  consumers. Source: `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts`.
- Note: This intake was auto-dispatched on an unclaimed/idea item; the seed
  description was judged sufficient to draft the brief without an interactive
  round (per intake § Interview "Skip the interview when seed context
  suffices"). The assumptions above are recorded for producer review.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** – Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item (completed)
- **WL-0MLUGOZO6191ZMWQ** – Improve sync test coverage (completed)
- **WL-0MMLT5UJC02BRTDB** – Finalize push rate-limit handling: create PR and tests (repro) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: abort, ac2, ac4, acceptance, accepts (+278 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: abort, accepts, add, adjust, agent (+251 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: abort, ac2, ac4, add, agent (+243 more)

# Guard fetchItemsByStage against invalid stages

## Goal

As a Herdr user, I want an invalid stage filter to fail soft rather than issue
a `wl list --stage <invalid>` call and show a misleading empty worklist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` `fetchItemsByStage` guards unknown/invalid stages fail-soft: it never issues `wl list --stage <invalid>` and never throws (returns an empty or fallback list).
- [ ] `STAGE_STATUS` no longer supplies a status mapping for the removed stages `in_progress`/`completed`.
- [ ] A regression test proves `in_progress`/`completed`/`bogus` cannot produce a CLI invocation and do not throw.
- [ ] Valid stages (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`, `done`) keep their existing status behaviour.
- [ ] `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts` no longer asserts that `fetchItemsByStage('in_progress')`/`('completed')` returns items.

## Minimal Implementation

- Validate the requested stage against the canonical `STAGES` list before calling `runWl`.
- Return an empty list for invalid stages without spawning the CLI.
- Update the fetcher regression tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
- `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/stage-status.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the STAGES alignment task (the canonical list is the validation source).

## Deliverables

- Fail-soft `fetchItemsByStage` plus regression coverage.
